title: Chapter 93
content:
The silence stretched endlessly.

Just say something, you bastard. Laugh in my face, mock me—do anything but stare at me with that completely dazed, struck-by-lightning look.

Jakyeong had swallowed every shred of his pride to spit out those words, yet the man’s reaction was entirely broken.

Finally shattering the quiet, Il-hyun didn't look at Jakyeong. Instead, he slowly turned his head toward Park Tae-soo, his expression practically glowing with celestial, breathless reverence.

"Tae-soo."

"Lee Ja-kyeong just proposed to me."

Jakyeong immediately shoved Il-hyun’s arm with a scowl. "Stop putting words in my mouth! I said I’d protect you. When the hell did I ask to get married?!"

Checking his diamond wristwatch, Il-hyun turned back to his security chief. "Delay the motorcade departure by thirty minutes."

Without another word, he clamped a massive hand around Jakyeong’s forearm, physically hauling him back toward the grand estate.

Jakyeong dug his heels into the gravel, thrashing to break the grip, but the man was an immovable freight train. Dragged through the front entrance before he could even kick off his sneakers, they charged up the grand staircase.

Hearing the commotion, the senior housekeeper poked her head out of the gourmet kitchen, her eyes widening in surprise.

"Keep everyone off the second floor," Il-hyun barked over his shoulder.

He dragged Jakyeong straight into the master suite at the end of the hall. He was in such a frantic, frantic rush that he tried to push open a door that pulled, rattling the frame violently before hissing a foul curse.

Jakyeong twisted his arm, demanding to know what kind of madness this was, but Il-hyun ignored him entirely—hauling him across the threshold, tossing him flat onto the king-sized mattress, and straddling his hips in one continuous, breathless motion.

Flustered, Jakyeong shoved against the broad, tailored chest, glaring in sheer bewilderment. "What is wrong with you?! Aren't you supposed to be heading to headquarters?!"

Buttons scattered across the hardwood like hail.

"You crazy bastard...!"

"What?"

"I told you this was my favorite shirt!"

The raw desperation in the man's tone felt so foreign. He truly was impossible to read. One moment he was colder than ice, the next an impeccably courteous gentleman, and now he was looking at him like a pathetic soul begging for a scrap of love.

No wonder I’ve lost my damn mind... leaving my guns behind and acting like an idiot.

For the first time in his life, Jakyeong realized that stroking someone’s hair could bring such a quiet, gentle warmth.

[Are you sure you'll be alright?]

Hearing that Jakyeong had abruptly cancelled his departure, Wang Han’s voice was laced with heavy, immediate concern.

Takeya Jun escaping custody was alarming enough, but underworld whispers indicated that a wave of elite international contractors had recently entered the country. While their specific client remained unconfirmed, the timing carried far too many unsettling implications to ignore.

[Should Ryun and I stay behind as well?]

"No. With Ryun’s condition, you'd only be dead weight. Take him to Honolulu and make sure he rests."

Han still sounded deeply reluctant to leave him alone in Seoul.

[The second anything feels off, call me immediately.]

"I will. Stop worrying."

Ending the call, Jakyeong stepped onto the terrace with a lit cigarette.

His phone chimed with an incoming photograph—Wang Han and Wang Ryun standing at the international departures gate. Ryun looked thoroughly despondent, his eyes glazed over and staring blankly into the distance.

Seeing the usually obnoxious giant so deflated left a sour ache in Jakyeong’s chest.

He exhaled a long ribbon of smoke, looking down into the courtyard.

Near the lawn, the senior housekeeper was playing fetch with Happy, the massive German Shepherd. She had always doted on the rowdy beast, and thanks to recent training, the dog was behaving far better than before.

Suddenly, Happy planted his paws, barking aggressively at the base of the perimeter wall.

The housekeeper walked over, hauling back on the leash. Even from the second-floor terrace, Jakyeong could see the triangular head of a viper reared up beneath the bricks.

Jakyeong leaned over the railing, debating whether to call security or head down himself.

Before he could move, the old woman casually reached down, snatching the serpent right behind the venom glands with blinding speed.

The hand speed was inhuman—an execution so clean and effortless it defied belief for a woman past sixty.

Jakyeong stared, his jaw practically hitting the floorboards.

She held the writhing snake up to show the dog, chuckled warmly, and tossed the reptile clean over the perimeter wall like a piece of yard waste.

Turning around with the leash in hand, her eyes caught Jakyeong standing on the balcony. She offered a cheerful, grandmotherly wave. Jakyeong managed a stiff, awkward smile before slipping back inside.

Catching a live pit viper with bare hands like it's a stray sock...

Come to think of it, when she buried Choi Ki-tae’s severed head in the garden, and when she found out he was a contract killer instead of Jang Yi-an, she had never batted a single eyelash.

Who the hell is that old woman...?

While he was spiraling in suspicion, his phone buzzed.

My Darling ♥

[Shall we go on a date tonight?]

The sugary, romantic phrasing made Jakyeong’s face twist into an immediate scowl. Fucking a man is disorienting enough, but a date?

Yet even as his pride rebelled, his brain was already betraying him—wondering what restaurant they’d go to, feeling like a total hypocrite. Am I catching his mental illness?

Before he could draft a reply, a follow-up text landed:

[See you tonight.]

He didn't even wait for an answer.

Chuckling at the man's arrogant presumption, Jakyeong began typing a short Okay.

Hovering over the period key, his thumb caught on the red heart emoji right above the keyboard.

Suddenly, the punctuation mark vanished, and the bright red symbol took over his vision.

No. Don't be an idiot.

His brain screamed to delete it, but his traitorous thumb betrayed him—hitting send on the bright red heart.

The instant the message cleared the outbox, a tidal wave of mortification crashed over him.

Fuck! Why did I send that?!

Panicking, Jakyeong hammered the screen, frantically hitting unsend.

He probably didn't see it. Yeah... He's a billionaire CEO. He's far too busy in executive meetings to check his screen.
